original_oracle.written_bar: behavior asserted against the ORIGINAL game's own natural execution, not injected state
original_oracle.basis: the fight law is measured end-to-end on NATURAL execution of a from-boot pinned movie (from_boot v4, armed_while_paused=true (phase_delay_owed handled by the v4 fix), 15600 frames, scene 14): spawn -> 15 damage events -> counter 0 by f7320, 1..7 through f10620, 8 at f11700; HP=0 at f11880 -> kill -> retirement, every writer an attributed PC, and the perch qualifier proved by breakpointing the predicate's own test instruction (15 evaluations, 8 scoring, 7 not). The FSM negative is a poll-only natural replay (138 IP samples, 2 distinct values). The row also has real executable assertion machinery, which F-rows generally lack: 12 declarative DuckStation scenarios (3 of them named as dependencies by the retained artifacts themselves) and 8 registered gate files
original_oracle.gap: three separate holes. (1) 9 of 71 tests in this row's 8 registered gate files fail on today's tree, across 6 of those files -- an oracle that does not run green is not an oracle today. (2) The row's headline identity binding is INJECTION by construction ('HP@+0x6e <= 0 retires the boss; HP=1 does not' via poke), and so are the 3 damage regimes and the soft-lock, which the closure artifact itself classifies 'perturbation_only_not_native_gameplay'. (3) Nothing in this row asserts the STAGE: a from-boot completion oracle for this stage already exists (movies/go_to_end/LEVEL09.movie.json, 12570 frames, pristine_replay_accepted=True) and the row does not cite it (cited=False)

lifecycle.written_bar: cold boot / load / first use / repeated use / exhaustion / retirement / reuse each evidenced
lifecycle.basis: this row has something most rows do not: a single COLD-BOOT natural arc covering most of the list in one fixture (from_boot v4, armed_while_paused=true (phase_delay_owed handled by the v4 fix), 15600 frames). Load is the spawn write at level load; first and repeated use are 15 damage events with 8 counted; exhaustion is the counter saturating at its target and the kill write firing there; retirement is instruction-bound at ['0x8004d270', '0x8004d43c'] and independently poke-falsified ('HP@+0x6e <= 0 retires the boss; HP=1 does not') with a complete, untruncated write log (30 events, truncated=False); and objective completion -> scene exit is causally isolated (suppressing only 0x800b3e84 leaves scene 14 loaded)
lifecycle.gap: reuse and reset are absent, and the row's own artifacts say so: 'Initialization, re-engagement, retry/checkpoint and persistence breadth remain open; only natural defeat/retirement/exit is bound.'. The arena half is worse -- its only runtime anchor is a LATE-PHASE save state (anchor_hp=0, phase_limit='late-phase only', movie_used=False), so early/mid-fight geometry timing, contact/damage timing and post-fight reset are unobserved; E11 lists 5 remaining promotion items and asks for exactly that fixture. cross_system_behavior.written_bar: native combinations exercised (carry+damage, powers+jump, projectiles at transitions, enemies vs hazards/plants)
cross_system_behavior.basis: five distinct native crossings are exercised on natural execution, each with a matched control and an explicit forbidden-claim boundary. PROJECTILE x BOSS: the boss takes damage through the ordinary berry dispatch, and the natively reachable delta is closed to [0, 2, 3, 4] (max 4). DYNAMIC GEOMETRY x PLAYER DAMAGE: 4 of 6 arena rows contact the player naturally for -1 health, the remaining 2 by threshold-only control at equal origin. BOSS ARENA x DEATH/LIVES: a row-4 contact made fatal on the final life yields [-1, 0, 2] (health/lives/master). REWARD DROPS x PICKUP ECONOMY: 7 volleys / 70 allocations produce 4 natural health pickups and 14 grain pickups. OBJECTIVE x SCENE TRANSITION: the completion request is causally isolated from the fade request and from retirement
cross_system_behavior.gap: no registered combination matrix exists, so 'native combinations' has no declared target set to measure against -- the five crossings are the ones the recording happened to contain. Two arena rows are control-only, the soft-lock crossing is 'perturbation_only_not_native_gameplay', and the canonical bar text names combinations (carry+damage, powers+jump) that this stage may or may not admit -- unresolved. A verifier decides whether crossings exercised without an enumerated target set can meet the written bar

The boss fight is the best-evidenced object in this row by a distance (from-boot natural fight law, instruction-bound writers, enumerated value domains, declarative scenarios and registered gates), and it belongs to D18; what F09 owns as a STAGE -- entry, layout, the arena's visible mapping, retry and reset -- is where every gap sits.

The authored count is right (1 sector, histogram {'0': 1}, rank 1 of 16 -- the campaign minimum, next lowest 12). The 45 is NOT Bug-Bar-specific: the runtime-registered tail is [45] in 16/16 levels -- a constant engine-side tail, not dynamic arena geometry. What IS distinctive survives the correction: at 45/46 this stage has the campaign's highest runtime-registered fraction (True), i.e. almost none of its collision environment is authored on disc.

THE ROW'S OVERLAY IS ATTRIBUTED TO THE WRONG FILE in the semantic registry. Every level overlay loads at the same VA, so the counter writer 0x800B3DB0 names a real instruction in 18 of the 20 censused overlay images; the ownership graph picks ['overlay:ambiguous']. Settled here from bytes: of 21 images (all overlays plus the resident EXE) exactly 1 contains the three fight-lane encodings once each with one consistent load base -- OVL/LEVEL04_LEVEL1.BIN @ 0x800b39a0, sha256 agreeing with D18's own overlay pin (True). Any future F09 work that resolves an overlay address by VA alone will land in another level.

THE ROW'S OWN GATES DO NOT RUN GREEN. 9 of 71 tests in this row's 8 registered gate files fail on today's tree, across 6 of those files. Two distinct causes, both measured: 6 of 36 self-declared dependency pins no longer match on-disk bytes (the central fixture manifest has legitimately been regenerated since), and the largest retained artifacts still assert the pre-correction scene routing, so the gate that recomputes routing now fails BECAUSE the project fixed the claim. Neither is evidence corruption; both mean the row's regression surface is not currently protecting it.

THE ROW UNDER-DECLARES ITS OWN EVIDENCE BASE. It declares 4 fixtures and cites 3 artifact paths, while the census credits 5 analysis artifacts and this assessment pins 13 that carry F09-labelled evidence -- including four large retained runtime artifacts (arena, completion, volley, defeat) that the baseline row never names.
